questions.prompt: Which part of a skill does Claude use to decide whether the skill applies to a request?

choices.C: The first heading of the instructions

questions.explanation: Claude matches the request against each skill's description; that is why the description is the trigger.

questions.prompt: You want a skill available in every project on your machine, but not shared with teammates. Where does it go?
questions.explanation: Personal skills live in ~/.claude/skills/ and follow you across projects; .claude/skills/ in a repo is shared with everyone who clones it.

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between CLAUDE.md and a skill?

choices.A: CLAUDE.md is loaded in every conversation; a skill loads only when a request matches
choices.B: Skills are always loaded; CLAUDE.md loads on demand

questions.explanation: CLAUDE.md is always-on context; skills are on demand, with only their name and description present until triggered.

questions.prompt: How does a skill differ from a slash command?

choices.A: Skills need to be typed explicitly
choices.B: Slash commands are chosen automatically by Claude
choices.C: A skill activates automatically when Claude recognizes a matching task; a slash command runs when you type it

questions.explanation: The course contrasts explicit invocation (slash commands) with automatic, match-based activation (skills).

questions.prompt: Give one concrete sign, from your own work, that something should become a skill, and say why.
questions.answer: Any recurring explanation you keep re-typing to Claude (review checklist, commit format, brand rules). It should be task-specific rather than always-true.
questions.explanation: The course's rule of thumb: if you explain the same thing repeatedly, it's a skill waiting to be written. Always-true rules belong in CLAUDE.md instead.

questions.prompt: At session start, what does Claude Code load from each discovered skill?

choices.A: The whole SKILL.md and all supporting files
choices.D: Nothing until you type the skill name

questions.explanation: Only name and description are loaded up front; the full SKILL.md is read after a match is confirmed.

questions.prompt: Put the skill sources in priority order, highest first.
questions.explanation: Enterprise (managed settings) wins, then personal, then project, then plugins.

questions.prompt: You cloned a repo with a project skill named code-review, and you also have a personal code-review skill. Which one is used?

choices.D: Claude asks which one every time

questions.explanation: Personal outranks project. The robust fix is to avoid generic names that collide.

questions.prompt: What happens right after Claude matches your request to a skill, before reading its full content?

choices.B: It asks you to confirm loading the skill

questions.explanation: The confirmation step keeps you aware of what enters the context; after that the full SKILL.md is read.

questions.prompt: Describe the minimal steps to create and verify a personal skill called changelog-writer.
questions.answer: Create ~/.claude/skills/changelog-writer/SKILL.md with frontmatter name: changelog-writer and a description saying what it does and when to use it, then the instructions. Start a new session, ask which skills are available to see it listed, then test with a natural request.
questions.explanation: Directory named after the skill + SKILL.md with name/description + instructions; new session; list skills; test with a realistic phrasing.

questions.prompt: Which name is valid for a skill?
questions.explanation: Names use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only (max 64 characters) and should match the directory name.

questions.prompt: A skill has `allowed-tools: Read, Grep`. During that skill, Claude decides it needs to edit a file. What happens?

choices.A: The edit is impossible while the skill is active
choices.B: The edit goes through the normal permission flow

questions.explanation: allowed-tools pre-approves the listed tools; it does not restrict others. Use disallowed-tools to actually remove tools.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum length of the description field?
questions.explanation: Description: max 1,024 characters. Name: max 64.

questions.prompt: Why tell Claude to run a bundled script rather than read it?

choices.B: Running it only puts the output in context, saving tokens and giving consistent results
choices.C: Scripts cannot be read on Windows
choices.D: It makes the skill trigger more often

questions.explanation: The script's source never enters the context; only its output does. Tested code is also more reliable than regenerated code.

questions.prompt: Your SKILL.md has grown to 1,400 lines, including a long API reference used only occasionally. How do you restructure it?
questions.answer: Keep the core workflow in SKILL.md (under ~500 lines); move the API reference to references/api.md (templates to assets/, helper code to scripts/); link each file from SKILL.md with a note saying when to read it.
questions.explanation: Progressive disclosure: SKILL.md acts as a table of contents, and details load only when needed.

questions.prompt: You want a linter to run every time Claude saves a file. What should you use?
questions.explanation: Hooks are event-driven: they fire on events such as file saves or tool calls.

questions.prompt: "Never modify the database schema" must hold in every conversation in this repo. Where does it belong?
questions.explanation: Always-on constraints go in CLAUDE.md; skills are for task-specific knowledge.

questions.prompt: What best describes the difference between a skill and a subagent?

choices.A: A skill adds knowledge to the current conversation; a subagent works in its own isolated context and returns a result
choices.D: Skills run in a separate context

questions.explanation: Skills join the current context; subagents are separate execution contexts for delegated work.

questions.prompt: Claude needs to query your company's ticketing system. Which feature provides that capability?
questions.explanation: MCP servers provide external tools and integrations; a skill can then describe how to use them well.

questions.prompt: Design a small setup for a team: TypeScript strict everywhere, a detailed PR review procedure, formatting on every save, and isolated security audits. Which feature for each?
questions.answer: Strict mode rule -> CLAUDE.md; PR review procedure -> skill; formatting on save -> hook; isolated security audits -> custom subagent (optionally with a security skill listed in its skills field).
questions.explanation: Each feature has its specialty, and they combine. Always-on -> CLAUDE.md, on-demand expertise -> skill, events -> hook, isolation -> subagent.

questions.prompt: Your skill only makes sense for one repository's codebase. What is the simplest way to share it with the team?

choices.B: Commit it to .claude/skills/ in that repo

questions.explanation: Project skills are shared through git; everyone gets updates on pull.

questions.prompt: Which method fits a general-purpose skill you want the wider community to install?
questions.explanation: Plugins are designed for distribution across projects and to people beyond your team.

questions.prompt: You delegate a task to the built-in Explore agent. Can it use your project skills?

choices.B: Yes, if you mention them in the prompt
choices.C: No, built-in agents cannot use skills

questions.explanation: Built-in agents cannot access skills. Only custom subagents that list skills in their frontmatter can.

questions.prompt: When are the skills listed in a custom subagent's `skills:` field loaded?

choices.A: On demand, like in the main conversation
choices.C: Only when the subagent calls them by name

questions.explanation: They are preloaded at subagent start, so list only skills that are always relevant to that agent.

questions.prompt: Security review must be identical for every developer in the company, and nobody should be able to override it. Which distribution route and why?
questions.answer: Enterprise managed settings: deployed organization-wide with the highest priority, so same-named personal/project/plugin skills cannot override it. Managed settings can also restrict plugin sources (e.g. strictKnownMarketplaces).
questions.explanation: The keyword is 'must': mandatory, consistent standards belong in managed settings.

questions.prompt: A skill passes validation but Claude doesn't use it when expected. What is the most likely cause?

choices.B: The description does not overlap how the request is phrased

questions.explanation: Matching is semantic; add the trigger phrases users actually say and test variations.

questions.prompt: Which layout will NOT load?
questions.explanation: SKILL.md must sit inside a named skill directory, not at the skills root.

questions.prompt: Which command helps you see skill loading errors?
questions.explanation: Run claude --debug and look for messages mentioning your skill name.

questions.prompt: A skill's helper script fails on a teammate's Mac with 'permission denied'. Fix?
questions.explanation: Scripts need execute permission; also use forward slashes in paths everywhere.

questions.prompt: You installed a plugin but its skills don't show up. Walk through your steps.
questions.answer: Clear the plugin cache, restart Claude Code and reinstall; if still missing, validate the plugin's structure (skills/<name>/SKILL.md, valid frontmatter); use claude --debug to look for loading errors.
questions.explanation: Cache first, then structure via the validator, then debug output.
